binders: An arbitrary measurable sample space Ω.
A probability measure μ on Ω.
A natural-indexed sequence X of real-valued functions.
A nonnegative real p used in real arithmetic.
hypotheses: The family X is mutually independent.
Every X_i has the same distribution as X_0.
conclusions: As N tends to infinity, the probability laws of the N+1-term centered and normalized sums converge to the standard Gaussian probability measure.
mathematical_definitions: The normalized sum is sum_{i=0}^N (X_i-p) divided by sqrt((N+1)p(1-p)).
Each law is the pushforward of μ by that normalized sum.
The limiting law is Gaussian with mean 0 and variance 1.
translation.proposition_plain_english: Any iid square-integrable real sequence with mean p and variance p(1-p), for fixed 0<p<1, has its centered normalized partial-sum laws converge to the standard normal law.

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The conclusion uses N+1 zero-based summands rather than N positive-indexed summands.
No Bernoulli-valued or two-point-support hypothesis appears; the target applies to any iid L2 sequence with the stated mean and variance.
The probability-measure topology must be the intended weak-convergence topology.
